title: Lesson 10: Baptism and the Lord's Supper
description: Jesus left His church two gifts, and He gave them to a room full of people who were about to fail Him. This lesson looks at what those two gifts are for and why a church shares them together.

blocks.text: You have spent this course growing up: loving your neighbors, your family, and your church family, serving with your gifts, standing firm, worshiping, giving, and guarding your heart. The last lesson of Growing Up ends at a table.

blocks.alt: Jesus breaking bread at the Passover table, surrounded by His disciples in an upper room

blocks.title: The Table He Longed For
blocks.text: On the night before the cross, Jesus gathered His closest friends around a Passover table in a borrowed upstairs room. He told them how much the meal meant to Him.
And he said to them, "I have earnestly desired to eat this Passover with you before I suffer."

Then He took the bread, gave thanks, broke it, and handed it to them. "This is my body, which is given for you." He lifted the cup. "This cup that is poured out for you is the new covenant in my blood."

Look around that table. Judas would betray Him before midnight. Peter would deny Him three times before sunrise. The rest would scatter into the dark. Jesus knew every bit of it, and He still longed to eat with them.
Both of the gifts in this lesson come from a Savior who wanted you at the table before you ever got it right.
10.1 - How does it change things to know Jesus wanted them at the table knowing they would fail Him that night?
Baptism: The Doorway You Walk Through Once

Baptism is going under the water and rising again in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit, after you have trusted in Jesus. It does not save you. It announces what God has already done in you.

Do you not know that all of us who have been baptized into Christ Jesus were baptized into his death? We were buried therefore with him by baptism into death, in order that, just as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, we too might walk in newness of life.
Going under, your old life is buried with Christ. Rising up, you walk in His new life. Your whole body says out loud what your heart already believes: I belong to Jesus now.

Here is something easy to miss. Before Jesus went into the grave, He went into the water. At the very start of His ministry He was baptized, and He had no sin to bury. He stepped into the picture of a death and a resurrection years before He lived it. Jesus gave the picture first, then did the work, and now you step into the same picture to point back at what He did for you.

From the church's first day, this was the believer's first step. When Peter finished preaching, about three thousand people believed, and those who received his word were baptized that same day (Acts 2:41). They did not wait until they had grown enough or cleaned themselves up.

Notice too that nobody baptizes themselves. Someone lowers you into the water and someone lifts you out, and a family stands around watching. It is the front door into a people, not a private decision you make alone.
If you have trusted Jesus and have never been baptized, hear this as an invitation and not a demand. You do not need to become a better Christian first. The doorway is for beginners.
10.2 - What is one honest reason you have not been baptized, or one thing that day still means to you?
The Lord's Supper: The Table You Return To

If baptism is the doorway you walk through once, the Lord's Supper is the table you come back to for the rest of your life. Jesus took the oldest meal in Israel's story and filled it with Himself. The bread is His body given for you. The cup is His blood poured out for you.

For I received from the Lord what I also delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night when he was betrayed took bread, and when he had given thanks, he broke it, and said, "This is my body, which is for you. Do this in remembrance of me." In the same way also he took the cup, after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant in my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in remembrance of me." For as often as you eat this bread and drink the cup, you proclaim the Lord's death until he comes.

The meal looks back to the cross, and it looks forward to the day you eat with Jesus face to face. It also looks around. One loaf is shared by many people, which is a quiet reminder that you were saved into a household. This is not something you do alone in your kitchen.
Come Ready
Paul told the Corinthians to examine themselves before they ate, and he warned that taking the meal carelessly brought real consequences. That sounds harsh until you see what it protects.

A meal you cannot take lightly is a meal that keeps calling you back to honesty. You know the table is coming, so you come ready. Not ready as in good enough, because nobody at the table has had a perfect week. Ready as in honest. You name your sin, you remember the cross, and then you eat.

That is not a bouncer at the door. That is a gift. Jesus gave His church something that puts an unhurried, regular pressure on you to stop pretending, for the rest of your life. The table was never a reward for the strong. It is food for hungry people who know where the bread is.
10.3 - What would you need to be honest about before you come to the table next?
Two Gifts That Preach

Both of these gifts preach. Baptism tells the gospel to everyone standing around the water, watching an old life go under and a new life come up. The Supper, Paul says, proclaims the Lord's death until He comes. Even while they are feeding you, they are telling His story to the people watching.
10.4 - Who has been watching you follow Jesus lately?
Growing Out from Here

With this lesson, the Growing Up course comes to a close. The next course is 203, Growing Out, where the branches begin to bear fruit. You will learn simple rhythms for blessing the people around you, sharing your story, and living on mission right where God has planted you.
Lesson 10 Review

Jesus gave His church two gifts, and He gave them first to people who were about to fail Him. Baptism is the doorway you walk through once: your old life buried with Christ, your new life raised with Him, in a picture He stepped into before you did. The Lord's Supper is the table you return to again and again, where coming honestly is part of the gift. One doorway, one table, one gospel you can see, feel, and taste.
